To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the 32P postlabelling assay is able to detect DNA adducts in tissue of germ-free and conventionally raised rats fed pectin-free and pectin-containing diet, and (2) there is an indication that DNA adducts are more frequently detected in the colon compared to the liver, kidney and lungs, and that the number of adducts increases with the degree of pectin esterification

the number and intensity of I-compounds in DNA of colonic mucosa of germ-free rats fed a diet containing low-esterified (DE 34%) pectin was higher than the number and intensity in DNA of colons from germ-free rats fed pectin-free diet, conventional rats fed low-esterified or conventional rats fed high esterified pects.

(1) pectins with a low degree of esterification induce the formation of more and more intense DNA adducts in the colonic tissue of rats compared to pectins with higher degrees of esterifications, (2) this induction is more pronounced in germ-free compared to conventional rats, ( 3) the formation of DNA adducts is more pronounced in the colonic than in the hepatic, renal and lung tissues of the same animal
